reasoning_traces.think:
PETSA introduces a dual adaptation framework where a large, frozen forecaster is complemented by small, trainable calibration modules. These modules operate on input/output spaces using low-rank transformations and gated activations. The core innovation lies in leveraging partial ground truth arriving after prediction to refine forecasts without retraining the entire model. This is mathematically expressed through a calibrated transformation: X̂^cali = X + (tanh(α⊙X)·W + b), where W = A·B is a low-rank factorization. The loss function L_PETSA = L_T + L_pt integrates both full (delayed) and partial (immediate) labels, weighted by Huber loss to mitigate outliers. The gating mechanism α allows variable-specific adaptation, while the low-rank structure ensures parameter efficiency. In GSE context, this translates to a frozen season model with a lightweight weekly calibration overlay, updating team-specific parameters using observed game outcomes. The failure mode occurs when the partial signal is too noisy or insufficient to guide adaptation effectively.
